title: Relevance-Contrast Bench: Multidomain Embedset Protocol
content:
Purpose
This doc describes a lightweight, repeatable protocol for onboarding embedding models for semantic search and clustering across multiple domains and languages. The focus is small-to-medium embedsets that balance automated metrics with human contrastive review. Use this for model acceptance gating before environment rollout (hosted/dedicated).

Quick summary of approach
- Build a multidomain query-candidate set with explicit positives, soft positives, random negatives, and hard negatives.
- Evaluate retrieval relevance (nDCG@10, MRR@10), pairwise clustering sanity (silhouette on per-domain clusters), and embedding stability (cosine drift) across languages.
- Run lightweight human contrastive checks: given one query, rank 5 candidates and label which are relevant and which are plausible confusers.
- Detect regressions with sliding-window baselines + effect-size threshold. Alert and block rollout when regressions exceed thresholds.

Data composition rules
- Domains: include at least 4 domains (docs/product-qa, ecom-catalog, support-tickets, open-web-faq). Each domain should contribute >=200 queries.
- Languages: target languages = [en, es, fr, de, pt, zh]. For each language include: 100 short queries (<6 tokens), 100 medium (6-20 tokens), 50 long (>20 tokens). If translations are synthetic, mark them (field in dataset) and sample review accordingly.
- Positives/negatives: for each query: 1 gold positive, 2 soft positives (partial overlap), 5 random negatives, 3 hard negatives (semantic but incorrect). Hard negatives should be curated from model nearest-neighbors of a baseline model to stress test.
- Size: target final embedset: ~8k-12k query-candidate pairs depending on project. For tiny proof-of-concept 2k pairs is acceptable.

Evaluation metrics and rationale
- nDCG@10: primary metric for ranked relevance. Report per-domain and aggregate (macro-average).
- MRR@10: helpful to capture head bias for simple queries.
- Recall@k (k=1,5,10): sanity for retrieval coverage.
- Silhouette score (cosine) per domain cluster: detects gross collapse where embeddings stop separating classes. Not meaningful for tiny classes; only use when domain cluster size >=50.
- Average pairwise distance drift: compare mean cosine similarity for positive pairs between candidate model and baseline. Large decrease means embeddings got less confident.
- Human contrastive accuracy: percent of times model top-1 is labeled relevant by raters in blind review. Use for final accept/reject gate.

Regression detection and gating
- Baseline: use last accepted model deployment as baseline (or a stable canonical baseline if none). Maintain a 30-day rolling aggregate of metric means.
- Gating rules (simple conservative defaults): block rollout if any of the following hold: (a) macro nDCG@10 drops by >3 points absolute; (b) per-domain nDCG@10 drops by >5 points for any domain; (c) silhouette drops >0.08; (d) human contrastive accuracy drops >4 percentage points.
- Monitoring alert: lower severity if drop is between 1–3 nDCG points (trigger engineering review), high severity if >3.
- Statistical test: pairwise bootstrap (1k resamples) on nDCG aggregated across queries. Report p-value and 95% CI. Prefer effect-size + CI over raw p-values.

Manual contrastive review workflow
- Sample 200 queries stratified by domain and language.
- Generate top-5 candidate list from the model under test. Present to raters blind (no model label). Ask: which of these are relevant? Also ask for severity/confuser label (plausible, slightly-relevant, irrelevant).
- Raters: at least 3 raters per query, majority vote decides. Track rater agreement (Krippendorff alpha). If alpha <0.6, escalate for dataset polish.
- Use a simple Google Form / Airtable export for labels. Keep original candidate ids, queries, and language tag.

Hard-negative construction procedure
- Run baseline model retrieval over a large corpus (domain-specific). For each query, save top 50 neighbors. Filter neighbors that are not the gold positive; these become a candidate hard-negative pool.
- From that pool, pick 3 per query prioritizing lexical overlap and embedding proximity to create difficult distinctions. Document selection rationale for each chosen hard negative (short note field).

Scripts and reproducibility
- Expected artifacts from script run: metrics.csv (per-query metrics), summary.json (flattened numbers), bootstrap_ci.csv, human_review.csv. All artifacts must be timestamped and include model git SHA, config (embedding dimension, quantization, normalization).
- Example command (pseudo):
  python run_embed_eval.py --queries queries.csv --candidates candidates.parquet --model model:embedding-v1 --out artifacts/run-20241101 --hard-neg-from baseline_model:embedding-v0 --bootstrap 1000
- CI-metric thresholds stored in repo: /eval-configs/relevance-thresholds.yaml. Keep PRs that change thresholds small and include rationale.

Reporting and dashboards
- Create a per-run doc with: run metadata, per-domain metric table, top 30 regression examples (query + baseline top1 + new model top1 + human labels), silhouette plots, drift histograms, and rater agreement summary.
- Push a simple JSON summary to the Redwood Console evals ingestion endpoint (internal) so the run shows up on the team dashboard. See linked_artifacts for ingestion script PR.

Checklist before accepting a model
- [ ] Embedset composition adheres to language and domain minimums.
- [ ] Hard negatives constructed and attached to dataset with selection rationale.
- [ ] Automated metrics computed and compared to baseline with bootstrap CI.
- [ ] Human contrastive review completed with alpha >=0.6.
- [ ] All artifacts uploaded and reproducible via run script.
- [ ] If any gating rule triggered, an owner writes mitigation plan and re-run is scheduled.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to weight languages in macro-average when customer footprint is skewed? (proposal: customer-specific weighting in later stages.)
- Consider adding embedding calibration checks for multilingual models (language-conditioned temperature). Need guidance from applied-ml research.

Notes to self / implementation hints
- When building the candidate pool, prefer Parquet with columns: id, domain, language, text, doc_id, chunk_id. Keep text hashes to detect accidental duplicates across languages.
- For produced artifacts, keep a lightweight descriptor file (flat key-values) to simplify ingestion by downstream dashboard.
- Slack thread for live run updates: #embed-evals (pin the run url).

References and links
- Confluence master page: confluence:embed-evals/RELEVANCE-CONTRAST
- Baseline retrieval script: github:https://github.com/redwood-inference/embed-eval-scripts
- Previous internal evals for clustering sanity: jira:APM-2130 (see linked ticket)

If you review this doc and want to add domain-specific constraints (e.g., healthcare/legal), add a short "sensitivity" section and escalate to security/compliance for dataset approval.

-- Aisha
(reviewer: Mateo Ruiz)
